driving_aspects.caveat: one session. The quickest pass through each zone came from different laps, and they may not all be possible together. A link between a habit and a zone time is a correlation over your laps, not a cause. The run from the start line to the first braking zone is a straight like the others.

trail_braking.basis: each corner's entry against your own laps this session; turn-in and the envelope come from your own data

brake_temperature.reason: the .ibt carries no brake-temperature channel, only line pressure; nothing is estimated in its place

trail_braking.caveat: one session. The brake thresholds (10% on, 5% off) and the turn-in rule (30% of the lap's own peak lateral g) are heuristics; a link between trail and entry time is a correlation over your laps, not a cause

input_response.basis: your inputs against the car's response, measured channel by channel

bands.reason: only 0 ticks at this much lock

input_response.caveat: one session, one car, one set of conditions; every threshold here is read off your own data rather than brought in from outside

hardware.basis: raw sensor channels across all laps in this session

pedal_noise_floor.caveat: sensor-wear early-warning baseline; trend needs multiple sessions. A brief spike is a heuristic: a brake reading above 5% that comes and goes within 50 ms with the throttle flat on both sides

steer_torque.note: absolute torque at the column. at_own_max_pct is the share of moving ticks within 1% of YOUR highest reading this session, not a hardware rating

hardware.caveat: single-session observation; hardware trends need history

fuel_fade.agreement: pace did not improve while fuel dropped
fuel_fade.weight_note: car got lighter by ~0.0 liters of fuel over the run

driving_style.style_observation: distinct gap between throttle release and braking
driving_style.note: signed gap: negative = brake applied before the throttle lift

fatigue_curve.finding: flat — negligible qualifying steering reversals in either third

report_card.caveat: one session; fingerprints firm up with history

balance.basis: expected yaw self-calibrated from this session's own low-slip data; no physics model
balance.method: least-squares k in yaw~=k*steer*speed; k absorbs wheelbase and steering ratio

brake_bias.note: brake bias is the front share of braking force; as a general mechanism more front bias leans the braking phase toward understeer and less toward oversteer. Compare it against the braking lean above — Proctor reports the value, it does not recommend a setting.

balance.caveat: single-session self-calibration; a poor fit (low r2) weakens every number here
balance.finding: divergences under braking lean understeer; divergences on throttle lean oversteer; divergences coasting lean oversteer

track_width.basis: every clean lap's own GPS path measured against the reference lap's
track_width.origin_note: add these back to convert any lap's Lat/Lon into the same metres frame: x = (lon - origin.lon) * 111320 * cos(origin.lat), y = (lat - origin.lat) * 111320
track_width.sign_note: positive is to the LEFT of the reference lap's direction of travel, negative to the right

summary.spread_note: the typical spread ignores the single widest and narrowest laps (10th to 90th percentile) — it is where your line usually sat

track_width.caveat: this is the road YOU used across these laps, not the track's width — the .ibt carries no kerbs, white lines or surveyed edges, and a band that narrows means you were repeatable there, not that the road did
